title: Fresh calorimetry trial does not identify which water mass is reused
summary: The stem gives two different water masses, then says the same water mass for the ice trial. The calculation silently reuses the first mass. Reusing the most recently stated second mass changes the result and can change the closest-option key.
recommendation: State explicitly that the solid is removed and a fresh water charge equal to the FIRST trial water mass is placed in the calorimeter. Give that mass numerically in every forward and inverse stem. Then recheck all six options, explanations and exports.

title: Three helical-orbit questions require an unphysical ordinary positive ion
confidence: High for an ordinary atomic ion
summary: The first helical dataset implies q/m=2.5e8 C/kg, about 2.61 times the proton charge-to-mass ratio. That is not consistent with an ordinary positive atomic ion. The mathematical keys do follow the stated ideal equations.
recommendation: Either identify the object as an ideal positive charged particle, without claiming it is an atomic ion, or choose mutually consistent ion/voltage/field/radius/pitch data and regenerate the three answers. Add a species plausibility check.
